answer: A new identity registers a quartz key, locks a 60-credit opal bond, and must earn 50 opal credits before activation. Each delivery is quartz-signed and hashed into the opal registry, which rejects reuse. A pulse check re-verifies one delivery per epoch; failure voids the credit and burns the bond. The kth identity pays registry fee of 10+2(k-1) credits, so 1,000 fakes pay 1,009,000 in fees, lock 60,000 in bonds, and owe 50,000 work units. Rented opal credit fails on signer mismatch. An honest agent pays one 10-credit fee, locks a refundable bond, and earns its 50 credits on first jobs.
